As a person who works in Medicaid claims processing. 

The complicated system of the doctor needed to enroll in the program, the individual needing to enroll separately prior to going, the clinic/hospital/group needs to be enrolled, the doctor needs to enroll as a member of that clinic, and then the procedure performed has to line up with the diagnosis code used. 

All of that can be done right. But, like Dr.Mike said “oh no, you didn’t include the RT modifier. All the information we have tells us that obviously it was done with that modifier. It’s denied now.” 

So even then to get it paid they have to resubmit all of the information again and still wait for it to get processed and if it’s an issue with their file due to something like a last name change or a new office location it’s even worse. 

None of these systems communicate. It’s a mess.

comments.text: The accent thing is actually an interesting intersection between linguistics and medicine. Accents happen because every language has its own set of sounds, which are just movements of the mouth/tongue/vocal chords. If a person has damage to the brain that makes it difficult for them to do the physical movements that certain sounds require, it can end up sounding like an accent of a language that doesnt have those sounds, since those speakers also struggle with the same sounds. So in that woman's case, it's not that she weirdly has a Chinese accent, but whatever damage occurred made it difficult to produce certain sounds that by sheer coincidence are also difficult for native chinese speakers.

comments.text:
Keeping your cool in customer service is such important advice (and yes, in America, even health insurance is essentially customer service). 9 out of 10 times, your frustration is actually with the company, not the person on the phone; it’s just easier to get mad at the employee because they are a real person you can actually talk to.
I saw this firsthand when the mother of my child was trying to fix her Amazon account. She was struggling to remember her old password and ended up yelling at the representative and hanging up. I found out later that there’s actually only one main customer service hub for them in India, and that guy was truly trying his best.
I called back, apologized to that same representative, and politely asked if there was any other way to verify the account. He sounded so relieved to be treated with respect. He told me, 'Yes, just give me the last four digits of the card on file.' We gave him the info, and he had her back in the account immediately. Being polite literally solved the problem that yelling couldn't.
